name: Antti Herlin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2010-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Finland's richest person, Antti Herlin, is chairman of Kone Corporation, the world's third-largest maker of elevators and escalators.
His great-grandfather initially invested in Kone in 1924, and Herlin served as CEO from 1996 to 2006.
Kone's products appear around the world in such places as Shanghai Hongqiao International Airport and Makkah Clock Royal Tower hotel in Saudi Arabia.
During his tenure as CEO, he expanded operations through acquisitions and alliances, and was given control of the firm as reward by his father Pekka.
Herlin holds shares in Finnish media firm Sanoma, owner of Finland's largest newspaper Helsingin Sanomat.
Herlin's son Jussi is Kone's vice chairman, and his daughter Iiris is on the board of directors.
forbes_facts: After his father's death, 3 of his siblings sued him over his larger stake. The dispute was solved in 2005, leaving the siblings with stakes in spinoff Cargotec.
Kone has taken its R&D underground, In 2017 they expanded the elevator test facilities in Tytyri to reach 350 meters (1150 feet) inside a working limestone mine.

name: Jean Coutu
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: The billionaire in the white lab coat, Jean Coutu founded the Canadian drugstore chain that bears his name.
In 2017 Coutu agreed to sell the publicly-traded company to European supermarket giant Metro for $4.5 billion in cash and stock.
Son of a pediatrician, he opened his first pharmacy in 1969, offering low prices, good customer service and extended hours.
Coutu, who was chief executive until 2002 and then again from 2005 to 2007, grew The Jean Coutu Group by acquiring many of his competitors.
The company was once a leading shareholder of U.S. drug store operator Rite Aid but sold the last of its stake in 2013.

name: Luca Ferrari
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Luca Ferrari cofounded Italian app developer Bending Spoons in 2013 with his three cofounders Matteo Danieli, Francesco Patarnello and Luca Querella. He is CEO.
The four friends launched Bending Spoons after working together on an unsuccessful, earlier startup Evertale, a note-taking app.
The Bending Spoons cofounders met while studying in Copenhagen, Denmark, and would later relocate to Milan, Italy, as their new startup took off.
The Milan, Italy-based startup struck on the strategy of buying apps and companies with a loyal audience where it sees the potential to overhaul its features and pricing.
Bending Spoons was largely bootstrapped until it raised its first major funding round in 2022 and made its first takeover of Evernote in 2023.

The company last raised $270 on a $11 billion in October 2025 to help fund its takeover of AOL and Vimeo. Bending Spoons is now Italy's most valuable startup and has bought, or taken private, a string of apps and startups like Meetup, Eventbrite, and WeTransfer.

name: Yu Zhuyun
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2023-2026); Hurun China (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Yu Zhuyun is the chairman and CEO of Central New Energy Holding Group, a business whose diverse interests span new energy, real estate and wellness.
Central New Energy went public on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2018.
Yu holds an MBA from Hong Kong Baptist University and an EMBA from Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business.

name: Alfred Gantner
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2016-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: Alfred Gantner is the cofounder of Partners Group, a Swiss private equity firm that manages more than $185 billion.
Gantner started Partners Group in 1996 after stints at UBS and Goldman Sachs, where he met cofounders Marcel Erni and Urs Wietlisbach.
The firm went public in Switzerland in 2006 and the trio each own roughly 5% of the stock.
Gantner earned his MBA from the Brigham Young University Marriott School of Management, Utah.
forbes_facts: In 2021, Partners Group banned its staff from using the word "deal," asking them to think more like founders and less like short-term investors.

name: Karthik Sarma
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Sarma founded hedge fund SRS Investment Management in 2006 after five years at Chase Coleman's Tiger Global and now manages $10 billion.
SRS owns 43% of Avis through common stock and equity swaps, and Sarma has served on the car rental company's board since May 2020.
Avis stock surged 456% in 2021, fueled by talk of adding electric vehicles to its fleet, which helped Sarma's flagship fund return 35%.
Sarma is an Indian immigrant who came to New York to get his master's at Princeton and spent three years as a consultant at McKinsey.

name: Wu Xiangdong
sec_insider_companies: BeOne Medicines Ltd. (ONC) - President and COO
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Hurun China (2008-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Wu Xiangdong is founder and chairman of liquor maker ZJLD Group, best known for its colorless spirits (baijiu) in China.
The company's Hong Kong IPO in 2023 valued it at $4.5 billion.
Wu also chairs Vats, a liquor store chain in China.
Vats is headquartered in Beijing and listed at the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2019.
Wu also started Jinliufu, a well-known baijiu brand in the country, more than 20 years ago.

name: Tang Yiu
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Tang Yiu founded footwear and sportswear retailer Belle International in 1981. Top brands in Belle's repertoire include Teenmix and Staccato.
The company went public on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2007.
He took Belle private and sold his stake in 2017, in a deal that valued the company at $6.8 billion.
He no longer has any role in the company.
Tang's investment firm Shine Works funded ParticleX, a Hong Kong-based startup fund cofounded by his son Clement in 2017. ParticleX ceased operations in 2024.

name: Mike Repole
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Mike Repole cofounded sports drink BodyArmor in 2011.
Coca-Cola bought 15% of BodyArmor in 2018, then purchased the rest in 2021 for $5.6 billion, the company's largest acquisition of a brand.
BodyArmor's investors included tennis star Naomi Osaka and the late Kobe Bryant, who discovered the brand while rehabbing from a torn Achilles tendon.
The son of a waiter and a seamstress, Repole studied sports management at St. John's before working in sales for a small company, Mistic Beverage.
Repole also cofounded Glaceau, maker of the popular brands Vitaminwater and Smartwater, which he also sold to Coca-Cola, in 2007.

name: Steve Case
sec_insider_companies: MAUI LAND & PINEAPPLE CO INC (MLP) - Director,TenPercentOwner; Inspirato Inc (ISPO) - TenPercentOwner
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2007-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Steve Case cofounded investment firm Revolution, which has invested in over 200 companies.
His Rise of the Rest tour funds startups from non-coastal states, stopping in cities to a host pitch competition for a $100,000 investment.
Revolution has also invested in restaurant chain Sweetgreen, fantasy sports firm Draft Kings and wine retailer Vinfolio.
In 1985 Case helped found Quantum Computer Services. He became CEO in 1991 and changed its name to America Online (AOL).
AOL merged with Time Warner in 2001 in a $164 billion deal that was eventually deemed one of the worst mergers in history.
forbes_facts: Born and raised in Hawaii, Case attended Punahou School, where Barack Obama went to high school. He later served on Obama's Council on Jobs and Competitiveness.
The Steve and Jean Case Foundation foundation created the Impact Investing Network Map to track transactions between investors and socially-conscious startup.

name: Ho Hung Anh
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: Ho Hung Anh is chairman of Techcombank, a large commercial bank in Vietnam that went public in 2018.
Ho and fellow billionaire Nguyen Dang Quang, whom he met while studying in Russia, are two close business partners whose interests are intertwined.
Ho started investing in Techcombank, in which Nguyen was already an investor, in 1995. They took control in 2006.
Together they control two big listed companies, Masan Group and Techcombank, a commercial bank, through Masan JSC, a holding company that they co-own.

Techcom Securities, the brokerage arm of Techcombank, went public on the Ho Chi Minh City Stock Exchange in October 2025. Masan Consumer, the group's consumer goods unit, listed on the bourse two months later.
forbes_facts: Ho started out trading goods between Eastern Europe and Vietnam in the 1990s.

name: Doug Ostrover
sec_insider_companies: BLUE OWL CAPITAL INC. (OWL) - Co-Chief Executive Officer
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Doug Ostrover is a cofounder and co-CEO of Blue Owl, an investment firm specializing in private credit with $250 billion in assets under management.
Ostrover started credit firm Owl Rock Capital in 2016. A merger with Dyal Capital as part of a SPAC deal formed Blue Owl and took it public in 2021.
Previously, Ostrover cofounded credit firm GSO Capital Partners, which Blackstone acquired for up to $945 million in cash and stock in 2008.
He stayed at Blackstone until 2015, helping GSO grow to $75 billion in assets under management by the time he left.

name: Darcie Glazer Kassewitz
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2023-2026)
forbes_bio: Darcie Glazer Kassewitz and her five siblings sold a quarter of their 68% stake in Manchester United to British chemicals billionaire Jim Ratcliffe in 2023.
The deal valued the team at $5.4 billion (net of debt). Their father, shopping mall magnate Malcolm Glazer (d. 2014), bought the team for $1.4 billion in 2005.
The Glazer siblings still own the NFL's Tampa Bay Buccaneers; their father acquired the franchise for $192 million in 1995, and it's now worth an estimated $5.2 billion (net of debt).
Darcie is chairman of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers Foundation and two other family charitable foundations.
Brother Kevin runs the family's real estate arm, Glazer Properties. Brothers Joel and Avram co-chair Man U. Joel also co-chairs the Bucs with brothers Bryan and Edward.

name: Andrei Krivenko
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Andrey Krivenko is the founder of VkusVill, one of Russia's fastest- growing retailers with 1,600 grocery stores.
In 2012 Krivenko launched his first four VkusVill (Taste Town) stores to sell fresh products with short shelf life.
A former CFO of Agama, the large Russian distributor of fish and seafood, he opened his first store Izbenka to sell fresh dairy products in 2009.
VkusVill was slated to go public on the Nasdaq and the Moscow Stock Exchange in 2022 but it was cancelled amid Russia's invasion of Ukraine.
According to the IPO prospectus, Krivenko planned to donate 20% of his shares in VkusVill to eight key executives.
